frames.title: Ad Framework: This Is Not [The Product]
frames.on_screen:
Canva slide titled 'THIS IS NOT [THE PRODUCT]'
Section 'WHY THIS AD WORKS':
1. THIS IS ANOTHER CLEVER WORDPLAY WHERE WE CALL THE PRODUCT SOMETHING IT IS NOT AT FIRST GLANCE, CREATING A CURIOSITY GAP THAT NEEDS TO BE FILLED, AND THEN BRINGING IT BACK AROUND
2. TO MOST PEOPLE, IT COMES ACROSS AS ANOTHER PROTEIN SHAKE, BUT THIS CAN BE LEVERAGED TO SHOW IT'S MORE THAN THAT*
*HOWEVER, IT HAS TO MAKE SENSE. DO NOT OVERSTRETCH IT, IF THE DOTS DON'T GET CONNECTED, AND THE AD WILL FLOP
Example ad image for Huel: 'This is a meal. Not a protein shake.' with callouts '40g protein', '27 vitamins + minerals', '400 calories', '17 meals for $2.65 per meal'.
frames.not_in_transcript: Bullet points under 'WHY THIS AD WORKS' verbatim; exact Huel callouts: '40g protein', '27 vitamins + minerals', '400 calories', '$2.65 per meal'.

frames.title: Ad Framework: Specific Pain Point Ad
frames.on_screen:
Canva slide titled 'SPECIFIC PAIN POINT AD'
Section 'WHY THIS AD WORKS':
1. THIS LEANS INTO A SAYING THAT IS OFTEN USED TO "OFFEND PEOPLE" AND IS A VERY SPECIFIC PAIN POINT, "MUFFIN TOP"
2. THIS ALSO CREATES A VISUAL IN THE PERSON'S MIND AND MAY EVEN HAVE THEM REFERENCE THE "MUFFIN TOP" THEY CURRENTLY HAVE
3. THEY THEN LEVERAGE A VERY STRONG PRICE SLASH TACTIC. ($36 $27)
Example ad for RYZE Mushroom Coffee: '2000 MG Adaptogenic Mushrooms', '$27 ($36 DEAL)', 'LOSE THE MUFFIN TOP FOR GOOD', '30-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE'.

'I'm recreating this ad because I saw that it did actually get traction, and I think this is a real pain point for this specific avatar around being in a deficit.
